data.current_summary: Get the brands and other details of a card
data.current_description:
Use this endpoint to get information about the card or network token that enables you to decideon the routing of the transaction and the eligibility of the card for the type of transaction.

If you include [your supported brands](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/latest/post/cardDetails__reqParam_supportedBrands) in the request, the response also tells you if you support each [brand that was identified on the card](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/latest/post/cardDetails__resParam_details).
 
If you have an API-only integration and collect card data, use this endpoint to find out if the shopper's card is co-branded. For co-branded cards, you must let the shopper choose the brand to pay with  if you support both brands.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve card brand and co-brand details
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves card or network token information including brand identification and co-brand detection. Accepts card data and an optional list of supported brands. Returns identified card brands, co-brand information, and whether each identified brand is supported by your integration. Use this endpoint to determine transaction routing eligibility and to prompt shoppers to select a brand for co-branded cards. Requires CardDetailsRequest with card data and optional supportedBrands parameter.

For more information, see [Donations](https://docs.adyen.com/online-payments/donations).
data.summary_suggestion: Process a donation using a donation token
data.description_suggestion: Processes a donation transaction using a donation token previously generated by a `/payments` request. Requires a DonationPaymentRequest containing the donation token and target donation account identifier. Returns the donation transaction result. This endpoint completes the two-step donation flow: first generate a token via `/payments`, then process the actual donation with this endpoint. See Donations documentation for complete integration details.

Improved version clarifies the operation's role in the donation workflow, specifies that a token from `/payments` is required, explains the request/response structure, and helps AI agents understand when to use this operation in the donation process.

data.current_description: Creates an order to be used for partial payments. Make a POST `/orders` call before making a `/payments` call when processing payments with different payment methods.

Must be called before `/payments` requests when splitting a transaction across different payment methods. Accepts a CreateOrderRequest with order details and returns an order object containing a unique order reference. The returned order reference must be included in subsequent `/payments` requests to associate payments with this order. Enables split payment workflows.

data.current_description: Cancels an order. Cancellation of an order results in an automatic rollback of all payments made in the order, either by canceling or refunding the payment, depending on the type of payment method.
data.description_suggestion: Cancels an order and automatically rolls back all associated payments. Accepts a CancelOrderRequest with the order reference. Returns a cancellation confirmation. Side effects: all payments in the order are reversed - uncaptured authorizations are canceled, captured payments are refunded based on payment method capabilities. This operation affects the state of all payments linked to the order.

data.current_description:
This operation takes the origin domains and returns a JSON object containing the corresponding origin keys for the domains. 
> If you're still using origin key for your Web Drop-in or Components integration, we recommend [switching to client key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication/migrate-from-origin-key-to-client-key). This allows you to use a single key for all origins, add or remove origins without generating a new key, and detect the card type from the number entered in your payment form.
data.summary_suggestion: Generate origin keys for domain authentication
data.description_suggestion: Generates origin keys for specified domains to enable client-side authentication in Web Drop-in or Components integrations. Accepts a UtilityRequest containing a list of origin domains and returns a JSON object mapping each domain to its corresponding origin key. Each origin key is unique to its domain and required for secure client-side payment form initialization. Note: Origin keys are legacy; Adyen recommends migrating to client keys for improved flexibility and single-key management across multiple origins.
